title: Verified Pay Receipts for Truck Driver Hiring
one_liner: Drivers upload settlement stubs and AI turns them into the true, receipts-backed pay per mile and per hour away from home for every carrier, sold as a hiring credential and as income proof for lenders.
customer: Honest mid-size carriers (50 to 1,000 trucks) that pay $6k to $15k to hire each driver and can't prove their pay claims are real. Secondary buyers are mortgage and auto lenders (bank-statement and non-QM brokers) who serve drivers.
problem: Recruiter ads say 'up to 75 cents a mile, $100k+' but realized pay is often 20 to 35% lower after unpaid or practical-versus-paid miles, unpaid detention, chargebacks and deductions. Driver turnover at big truckload carriers runs near 90%, and job ads are so discredited that honest carriers can't stand out. Drivers whose pay is structured as tax-free 'per diem' also see a low W-2 and get denied mortgages after 20 years of work. Estimates say the English-proficiency and non-domiciled CDL crackdowns will pull 214,000 to 437,000 drivers (5 to 12% of CDL holders) from the supply over 2 to 3 years, so carriers are competing harder for domestic drivers.
solution: A mobile app where drivers photograph settlement stubs and pay statements. AI extracts paid miles, deadhead, detention, deductions, per diem and time away from home, and computes effective take-home per hour on the road, not just per mile. Public carrier pages show verified figures such as '312 verified drivers, median $0.61 per paid mile, $17.40 per hour away'. Carriers that look good pay for a 'Verified Pay' badge and applicant funnel. A second product builds an income-verification packet from stubs and deposit statements for lenders. Fraud controls include stub-format checks, duplicate detection and consistency with driver-reported miles.
why_now: Shrinking driver supply from the 2025 to 2026 English-proficiency out-of-service enforcement (proposed codification rule published Aug 10, 2026) and the Feb 2026 non-domiciled CDL restrictions means cost-per-hire is rising. Vision-model OCR of messy pay stubs is now cheap and accurate. Truth-in-leasing rules already require itemized settlements, so the raw material exists.
revenue_model: Carrier subscriptions of $500 to $3,000 a month for the verified page, analytics and applicant funnel. Lender referral fees of $300 to $1,000 per funded mortgage or truck loan. Free for drivers, which keeps the data supply growing.
non_obvious_insight: Drivers don't compare carriers by ads, they ask in the truck-stop lot 'what do you actually clear?' The only artifact they trust is a pay stub. The honest carriers are the ones locked out of trust, so they are the natural paying customer. The true unit of pay is dollars per hour away from home, because 14-hour clocks, detention and unpaid waiting eat the mileage math. And per-diem income structures are a hidden mortgage trap that a stub-based income packet can fix.
first_30_days: Post in trucker Facebook groups, Reddit and TikTok: 'Upload your stub, see your real rate vs. what your carrier advertised.' Aim for 500 stubs in 30 days. Publish a 'State of Real Pay' report ranking 20 named carriers and pitch it to trade press (Overdrive, CDLLife, FreightWaves). Sell 'Verified Pay' badges to the 5 mid-size fleets whose numbers look best, and sign one bank-statement mortgage broker for lender leads.

tournament.cluster: Gig, tipped and cash workers unable to prove income
judge_notes: operator: rank 9/25 - Carriers pay heavily per hire and drivers trust stubs; but two-sided data supply is slow and legally fraught.
contrarian: rank 4/25 - Stub-verified pay per hour away from home is a sharp insight; driver-supply squeeze makes honest carriers pay.
vc: rank 1/25 - Verified-stub pay data is a real wedge; carriers pay to hire, driver supply is shrinking, and the data moat compounds.

competitors.name: TruckersReport (carrier reviews and salary survey)
competitors.what_they_do: Largest trucker community and job board. Has carrier reviews (home time, equipment, management) and a driver-submitted salary survey ('Help fellow truckers know how much they should be paid'). Fetched pages show no verification method, no pay-stub proof and no per-carrier verified figures. It earns money from carrier job postings and recruiting partnerships, so it has a conflict of interest on carrier ratings. It is the closest thing to a direct competitor, and it could add a 'verified' layer.
competitors.scale_or_funding: Claims about 400 driver hires a month through the site (homepage). Funding not found.

competitors.name: Best Fleets to Drive For (CarriersEdge)
competitors.what_they_do: Annual survey and contest that ranks for-hire carriers on driver experience. Drivers nominate, and it is free for fleets (10+ trucks). This is the incumbent way an honest carrier signals it is a good employer. The page fetched does not say whether pay is verified, and I could not confirm that pay is examined at all.
competitors.scale_or_funding: Established program run by CarriersEdge, a training company. No funding data found.

competitors.name: Tenstreet (Driver Pulse, IntelliApp, Hiring Center)
competitors.what_they_do: Dominant recruiting and applicant-tracking platform for trucking carriers. It includes a Driver Pulse app, a job store, employment verification and fraud prevention. No pay-transparency or verified-pay product appeared on the fetched page. It owns the carrier recruiting workflow and the driver audience, so it is both a possible channel partner and the biggest risk of copying the idea.
competitors.scale_or_funding: Driver Pulse claims over 480,000 active users a month. Funding not found.

competitors.name: Drive My Way
competitors.what_they_do: Funded driver-to-carrier matching platform with 'matchmakers' and matching across 20+ attributes. The fetched page has no pay transparency or verified-pay feature. It shows that venture money flows into driver recruiting, and it is a plausible acquirer or partner.
competitors.scale_or_funding: Raised $44M (per the site's news mention). Partners include NFI, Republic Services and Mondelez.

competitors.name: Truv
competitors.what_they_do: Income verification from payroll, employer and bank connections. It has self-employment income and document-upload products, and serves mortgage, auto and consumer lenders. It has no trucking-specific product on the fetched page. It is the lender-side incumbent category, and a driver-uploaded stub packet is weaker than direct payroll data.

competitors.name: Argyle
competitors.what_they_do: Income, employment and asset verification for mortgage and personal lenders through payroll and platform connections. It has a Gig Economy solution using work activity and contract earnings. Trucking is not called out on the fetched page.
competitors.scale_or_funding: Venture-backed. Details not verified this session.

competitors.name: Gridwise
competitors.what_they_do: Earnings-tracking app for gig drivers that aggregates income and mileage across Uber, DoorDash and others. It has a B2B analytics product. It shows a driver-side earnings-tracking model works in gig work, but it does not cover trucking, lender verification or employer pay transparency.

competitors.name: Trucker Path
competitors.what_they_do: Dominant trucker app for navigation, truck stops and a load board. Its homepage shows no carrier reviews or pay data. A large community that could add a pay module.

competitors.name: Glassdoor / Indeed company salary and review pages
competitors.what_they_do: General employer-review sites with self-reported pay by company, including truck driver roles. I could not fetch either site (403), so this is from prior knowledge and not verified. As I understand it, the data is self-reported and not receipts-backed, and it is not shaped around trucking pay units.

competition.white_space:
Web search was unavailable (the session's 200-search budget was used up), so this rests on about 25 direct page fetches plus prior knowledge. Confidence is moderate to low. A reviewer should re-run searches for 'verified driver pay', 'settlement stub scanner' and 'trucker mortgage per diem' before committing.

I found no product that does all of this: (1) collect settlement stubs, (2) verify them with fraud checks, and (3) publish per-carrier, receipts-backed effective pay, including dollars per hour away from home. The closest, TruckersReport, has an unverified self-reported salary survey run by a site paid by carriers' recruiting budgets. Best Fleets to Drive For is survey-based. Tenstreet and Drive My Way own recruiting flow but show no pay-verification product.

Specific unserved gaps:
- A trust-backed pay number that uses stubs as proof, computed as dollars per hour on the road rather than per mile.
- Lease-purchase and owner-operator drivers, whose settlements are itemized and who are the most exposed to deceptive ads.
- A stub-based income packet that handles per-diem structures for non-QM and bank-statement lenders. Truv and Argyle verify through payroll connections and are not built for per-diem trucker income.

Weak points that could still sink it:
1. Cold start and selection bias. Unhappy drivers upload more, and carriers with a bad median will not buy a badge. A pay-for-badge model also has a credibility conflict.
2. Stubs do not show time away from home. Hours-away metrics need driver-entered dates or ELD integration, which is hard.
3. The truth-in-leasing itemized-settlement rule (49 CFR 376.12) applies to owner-operator leases, not W-2 company drivers. The idea's 'raw material already exists' claim is only partly true. I could not fetch the regulation this session.
4. Publishing rankings of named carriers invites legal threats. Self-published analytics are not covered by Section 230 the way user reviews are.
5. Per-funded-loan referral fees to a non-lender may run into RESPA Section 8, so this needs counsel. Lenders will also likely re-verify borrower-supplied stubs, which limits the lender product's value. This is from prior knowledge and not verified.
competition.evidence_of_demand:
Partial and mostly indirect, because searches were blocked.

Found:
- Drivers want peer pay data. TruckersReport runs a driver-submitted salary survey ('Help fellow truckers know how much they should be paid'), but it is unverified and shows no per-carrier verified figures: https://www.thetruckersreport.com/truck-driver-salaries/
- There is a large reachable audience. Tenstreet's Driver Pulse claims over 480,000 monthly active users (https://www.tenstreet.com/) and Trucker Path claims over 1M monthly active users (https://truckerpath.com/).
- Money flows into driver recruiting. Drive My Way raised $44M for driver-carrier matching (https://www.drivemyway.com/), and TruckersReport monetizes carrier job postings (https://www.thetruckersreport.com/).
- Carriers invest in being seen as good employers. Best Fleets to Drive For is a free annual contest (https://www.bestfleetstodrivefor.com/).
- Lenders pay for income verification: Truv reports 200+ customers (https://www.truv.com/).

Not found or not verified:
- No forum threads, RFPs or complaints about deceptive pay ads were retrieved. Reddit and OOIDA fetches were blocked.
- No evidence carriers will pay $500 to $3,000 a month for a verified-pay badge.
- No evidence lenders pay for a trucker-specific stub packet.
- The idea's claims of about 90% turnover, $6k to $15k cost per hire, and 214k to 437k drivers leaving supply are unverified by me. The ATA and ATRI pages I fetched did not surface those figures.
competition.sharper_angle:
Lead with a driver-side settlement auditor, not a carrier ranking site. Give drivers a reason to upload stubs that has nothing to do with the public database:
- Show them what they actually cleared per hour away from home.
- Flag unpaid or practical-versus-paid miles, unpaid detention and chargebacks.
- Output a dispute-ready summary.

Start with lease-purchase and owner-operator drivers. Their itemized settlements are easier to parse and they are the most exploited segment. Anonymized aggregates then build the receipts-backed pay index as a byproduct, which fixes the cold start.

For the carrier side, avoid a pay-to-play badge. Sell 'verified pay claims' that work like this:
- The carrier attests its advertised pay, and the platform checks the attestation against carrier-supplied settlement or TMS exports plus a driver stub sample, with published methodology.
- The result is embeddable in job ads through Tenstreet, Indeed or Drive My Way instead of competing with them.
- Prefer a flat SaaS or audit fee, with public methodology, over selling badges only to carriers that look good.

Defer or drop the lender product until there is stub volume. If it is kept, narrow it to a per-diem-aware income reconstruction for non-QM and bank-statement brokers, sold as a flat marketing fee and not a per-funded-loan referral, pending RESPA counsel.

Before building, run a 30-day stub-collection test. If about 500 stubs cannot be gathered from drivers with no payout, the model fails, and it fails cheaply.
